packages.label: צַדִּיקִים, רוֹעֶה, וּמֹשֶׁה
packages.label_en: The Tzaddikim, the Shepherd, and Moses
packages.reason: This is the largest connected component (3 nodes, 2 edges). כל הצדיקים שבדור and משה are both directly connected to רועה via bechina edges. The Rebbe states that every tzaddik in the generation IS a bechina of 'shepherd,' and the shepherd (the tzaddik of the generation, Moses archetype) IS a bechina of Moses — רְעָיָא מְהֵימָנָא, the faithful shepherd. All three nodes share the same essential nature: the tzaddik who collects good points from every Jew and thereby constructs a Mishkan (tabernacle) through which children receive their pure breath of Torah. Moses is the archetype of this function — collecting, gathering, shepherding the flock. The bechina is: what IS a tzaddik? He is a shepherd. What IS a shepherd? He is Moses. These three are three faces of the same spiritual reality.

packages.label: נִגּוּן וּבֵרוּר הַנְּקֻדּוֹת הַטּוֹבוֹת
packages.label_en: The Melody and the Extraction of Good Points
packages.reason: Two nodes (2-node component, 1 edge). The Rebbe states that playing a melody on an instrument IS a bechina of extracting the good spirit from the spirit of sadness and depression. The player of nigguns and the act of sorting/extracting good points from bad are the same spiritual act — both are expressions of the same essential operation: separating and elevating the holy spark from within the mixture of good and evil. This is not cause-and-effect (the niggun does not produce the extraction — they are the same thing described from two angles). The proof text explicitly uses 'הוּא בְּחִינַת': 'מְנַגֵּן בִּכְלֵי זֶמֶר, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שֶׁמְּלַקֵּט הָרוּחַ טוֹבָה מִן הָרוּחַ נְכֵאָה עַצְבוּת רוּחַ'. Melody IS the extraction. This is the musical/spiritual face of the core practice of Torah #282.
nodes: מלקט הרוח טובה מן הרוח נכאה עצבות רוח
merge_notes: This 2-node component is retained as a separate package rather than merged into Package 3 (the 'עוד מעט' cluster). While the practice of finding good points and the practice of making nigguns are deeply linked in the Torah's teaching (and are connected via eitza: finding good points PRODUCES nigguns), they are not the same essential nature. The niggun IS the extraction process (bechina: identical nature) — but the niggun/extraction is not the same thing as 'the good point found within the sinner' (עוד מעט). The niggun is the RESULT of gathering good points. This is an eitza connection between Package 2 and Package 3, not a bechina merging them. Keeping separate also preserves the teaching's own structure: the Rebbe introduces the music passage as its own conceptual station (citing LM #54).

packages.label: עוֹד שֶׁלִּי וְעוֹד מְעַט וְאֵין רָשָׁע
packages.label_en: My 'Still' and 'Yet a Little While and There Is No Wicked'
packages.reason: Two nodes (2-node component, 1 edge). The Rebbe interprets the Psalm phrase 'אֲזַמְּרָה לֵאלֹקַי בְּעוֹדִי' (I will sing to my God while I still exist) and draws a bechina between 'עוֹד שֶׁלִּי שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹצֵא בְּעַצְמִי' (the 'still' that I find within myself — the remaining good point) and 'עוֹד מְעַט וְאֵין רָשָׁע' (yet a little while and there is no wicked, Psalms 37:10). Both refer to the SAME thing: the small residue of goodness that remains in every person, the 'נְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה' (good point). The subjective experience of finding goodness in oneself ('עוד שלי') IS the objective reality that the verse describes ('עוד מעט ואין רשע') — they are two sides of the same coin. The bechina is symmetrical: just as the Psalm says there is always 'a little bit' of non-wickedness, so too the person's 'I still find something good in myself' is that very same reality viewed from within.
merge_notes: This 2-node component could in principle be merged with Package 2 (niggun/extraction), since finding good points IS the pre-condition for making nigguns. However, the connection between them is eitza (cause-effect: finding the good point leads to/produces the niggun), not bechina (they are not the same essential nature). The 'good point found in oneself' and 'the melody created from it' are two different things — the point is the raw material, the melody is the refined output. They belong to different packages. Package 3 is retained as the foundational conceptual cluster: the 'something good' that can always be found — the theological ground of the teaching.

stats.notes: Torah #282 has a small bechina subgraph with only 4 edges forming 3 separate connected components. No merges across components are warranted — each pair/triplet represents a distinct conceptual domain. The three packages correspond to three conceptual pillars of the teaching: (1) the tzaddik/shepherd/Moses as the vehicle of redemption, (2) the melody/extraction as the method, and (3) the 'good point' as the theological foundation. The eitza (cause-effect) chain flows: [Package 3: finding good points] → eitza → [Package 2: nigguns created] → eitza → [Package 1: tzaddik uses this to pray for and gather the flock]. No evil mirror package exists in the dataset for Torah #282, though the teaching's evil counterpart (the בעל דבר who tries to induce sadness/depression) is described in the text.
